latest_final: The father's daughter died of illness and was buried according to the village's ordinary custom. Because the village buries its dead in a forest burial ground that lies within the brown bears' territory, and bears—though wary of living humans and rarely attacking them—readily scavenge carrion in their habitat, a bear dug up her grave and was eating her buried body when the father found it. The father understood that the bear had not hunted or killed a living person; it had merely found and consumed a buried body left in bear country. Knowing that all the villagers' relatives are buried in that same ground, and that human bodies buried there are effectively food available to the bears, he fears those other buried loved ones will likewise be dug up and eaten—so that other villagers will suffer the same horror and grief of having a relative's body consumed.
